name: sidebar
title: Sidebar
description: App navigation: a named landmark with groups and items (href or a router link), the current page marked with aria-current, collapsing to an icon rail with tooltips (or hiding, with collapse="hide") and opening in a drawer on narrow screens. Agents collapse and expand it by name. A SidebarTrigger toggles it from elsewhere, like a Topbar, through its controller; useSidebarState wires both and remembers the state.
docs: Put a `SkipLink` first in `<body>`, before the `Sidebar`, so keyboard users can jump past the navigation, and give the page content the target: `<SkipLink>Skip to content</SkipLink><Sidebar …/><PageLayout as="main">…</PageLayout>` (PageLayout renders `<main id="main">`). If your shell renders `<main>` itself, give it `id="main"` (and `tabIndex={-1}`, so the no-JavaScript fallback moves focus too), or pass the SkipLink a `target` id or ref. To toggle it from a `Topbar`, pass one `createSidebarController()` to both: `<Topbar leading={<SidebarTrigger controller={sidebar} collapsed={collapsed} />} /><Sidebar controller={sidebar} collapsed={collapsed} onCollapsedChange={setCollapsed} trigger={false}>…</Sidebar>`. `collapsed` gives the trigger `aria-expanded` and the name of the next step; without it the trigger is named "Toggle sidebar". On narrow screens it opens the Sidebar's drawer (named "Open navigation", `labels.open`), and a Sidebar with `trigger={false}` renders no drawer button of its own (`narrowTrigger` overrides that); give both the same `narrowQuery`. `useSidebarState({ storageKey })` returns the controller and the state for both, remembered in localStorage: `const sidebar = useSidebarState({ storageKey: "app-sidebar" })`, then `<SidebarTrigger {...sidebar.triggerProps} />` and `<Sidebar {...sidebar.sidebarProps} trigger={false}>`. Give a sidebar whose items have no icons `collapse="hide"`: collapsed, it slides away instead of leaving an empty rail.
